I have farmed this land since I was a boy, and I keep cattle, so I put manure on this plot every year because it is mine and I want the soil to stay good. Last season my nephew used urea on his sorghum and the stalks grew thick, so I will buy five bags of urea to spread thin across these 7.81 hectares — it is not much for such a big piece, but it is what my cash allows. I use my own saved seed, sorghum mixed with cowpeas like always; I do not trust shop packets or chemical sprays, and we have no water for irrigation here. My family will work about 150 days on this plot, and I will hire young men from the village for about 220 days because at 64 years old I cannot dig all this ground alone.
